facts: A framework for segmentation of complex scenes was previously presented.
The previously presented framework uses multiple physical hypotheses.
The multiple physical hypotheses are for simple image regions.
A consequence of the previously presented framework was a proposal for a new approach.
The new approach is to the segmentation of complex scenes.
The new approach segments complex scenes into regions corresponding to coherent surfaces.
The new approach is contrasted with segmenting into regions of similar color.
An implementation of the new approach is presented.
Example segmentations are shown for scenes containing multi-colored piece-wise uniform objects.
The scenes contain multi-colored piece-wise uniform objects.
The piece-wise uniform objects are multi-colored.
The new approach intelligently segments scenes with objects of greater complexity than previous physics-based segmentation algorithms.
Using general physical models yields segmentations that correspond more closely to coherent surfaces in the scene than segmentations found using only color.
General physical models are used to obtain segmentations.
Segmentations found using only color correspond less closely to coherent surfaces in the scene.
